mainEntity.name: How long is a normal menstrual cycle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under FIGO's 2018 definitions, a normal adult cycle is 24 to 38 days long, counted from the first day of one period to the first day of the next.

mainEntity.name: Why did my period come early or late?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stress, illness, travel, weight changes, intense exercise and some medicines can shift ovulation, which moves your next period. A single early or late period is common; a persistent change is worth discussing with a doctor. If you could be pregnant, take a pregnancy test.
They're most accurate for regular cycles. Even then, a few days either way is normal. Using your average from several recent cycles improves the estimate.
